factsheet_lines_1_indexed.3: - *Martha Larkspur*: Local baker, custard specialist, and multiple-time winner of the Pie Festival's custard category.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.4: - *Allan Simms*: Local detective with a doctorate in chemistry, known for his methodical and scientific approach to investigations.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.5: - *Birchtown Festival Committee*: Organizers of the annual Pie Festival, responsible for rule revisions post-heist.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.6: - *Pie Festival Participants*: Various local and visiting bakers who participate in the annual Pie Festival.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.7: - *Mysterious Saboteur*: Unidentified person or persons responsible for the custard switch.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.11: - *Custard Preparation*: Months leading up to the festival, Martha Larkspur prepares her renowned custard, incorporating a secret ingredient.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.12: - *Opening Day Disappearance*: On the opening day of the festival, Martha discovers her custard missing, prompting an investigation.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.13: - *Investigation by Allan Simms*: Detective Simms is called in to investigate; he utilizes his chemistry background to analyze the contents of the replacement custard.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.14: - *Discovery in the Trophy Case*: The missing custard is found stashed in the festival's prize trophy case, and the replacement custard is declared unsuitable.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.15: - *Rule Revision by Festival Committee*: In response to the scandal, the festival committee revises competition rules to prevent future incidents.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.16: - *1954 Pie Festival*: The heist adds intrigue, making it the most memorable festival in Birchtown's history.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.20: - *Birchtown*: Small, serene town known for its annual Pie Festival.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.21: - *Larkspur Bakery*: Martha Larkspur's bakery, where the custard was originally prepared.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.22: - *Festival Grounds*: Location of the Pie Festival, where the heist took place.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.23: - *Trophy Case*: Where the missing custard was discovered.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.27: - *1954*: Year of the Great Custard Heist.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.28: - *Months Leading Up to the Festival*: Time period during which Martha Larkspur prepared her custard.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.29: - *Pie Festival Opening Day*: Day when the custard was reported missing.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.33: - *Secret Ingredient*: Martha's custard contained a rumored secret ingredient that guaranteed a win, making it a target for sabotage.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.34: - *Fair Competition Concerns*: The heist highlighted the need for fair competition and transparency in contest entries.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.35: - *Festival Committee's Response*: The scandal prompted rule revisions to ensure integrity and prevent future incidents.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.36: - *Intrigue and Memorability*: The heist added drama to the festival, embedding it in Birchtown’s collective memory as a notable event.

items.instruction: Under the confirmation rules a preserved unit (assertion_only or conflict_flagged) must be its own group, and that group's statement must be the unit's source_statement copied verbatim, with no added or removed punctuation. Fix it in one of two ways. (a) Only for assertion_only: if an exact factsheet line supports the assertion as stated, set status "grounded", give the exact line(s) as evidence, and say why in "note". The unit may then stay in its group. (b) Otherwise give the unit its own group: a new id ground-<event>-<nn> with an unused nn, source_unit_ids [the unit], statement = source_statement verbatim, and a grouping_rationale. Remaining members keep their group. Every distinct answer label of every group must have exactly one source_qa record with two closed-book questions (AUTHORING-SPEC.md). Move, keep or write source_qa records so this holds, with unit_id set to the record's group id. For this item, option (b) means setting this group's statement to the source_statement verbatim. Then check that its source_qa questions still follow the rules.
